title: PM spec alignment: customer-facing overload behavior (HTTP semantics, messaging, compat/deprecation)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Goal
Align Product + SRE + Platform on customer-facing behavior during overload so we:
1) prevent ambiguous failures (timeouts/5xx soup),
2) provide stable/consistent error semantics across REST + OpenAI-compat + streaming,
3) preserve backwards compatibility expectations and document any deprecations.

Context
We are introducing layered circuit breakers + load shedding across gateway → routing/control plane → runtime/GPU pools. This ticket is the PM-owned spec alignment for the external contract: status codes, error codes, headers, body shape, retry guidance, and messaging principles.

Primary consumers
- Customer application developers (direct REST + OpenAI-compatible clients)
- SDK users (Python/TS/Go)
- Support/CS and Oncall (need crisp guidance and consistent terminology)

Non-goals
- Defining internal breaker thresholds/hysteresis (SRE owns; see ENG-4828)
- Replacing quotas/rate limits (existing mechanisms remain; overload protection complements)
- Designing new customer-specific bespoke overload logic (we provide primitives + safe defaults)

Decision summary (what we are standardizing)
A) HTTP status codes and when they appear
1) 429 Too Many Requests (preferred for “try again soon” conditions)
- Used when we intentionally shed requests due to temporary capacity pressure and we expect recovery on a short time horizon.
- MUST include Retry-After (seconds) and a stable Redwood error code in body.
- MUST be returned consistently at all entrypoints that can shed early (gateway), and when routing/runtime return a shed reason.

2) 503 Service Unavailable (used when service or region/model tier is degraded/unavailable)
- Used when a breaker is open for a (model, region, tier) due to sustained overload or brownout.
- SHOULD include Retry-After when meaningful. If unknown, omit rather than provide misleading values.
- Returned for “no capacity” and “breaker open” conditions where immediate retries would amplify load.

3) 499/504/5xx handling principles
- We should reduce 5xx/timeouts that are symptoms of overload (queue blowups, scheduler collapse). Overload-protected requests should not show as generic 500/502/504.
- If we must terminate long-running requests (esp. streaming) for platform stability, the client-visible error should still map to a standard overload semantics where possible.
- Any internal 5xx due to genuine bugs or unexpected failures remain 5xx (and count toward error budget differently; see SLO policy update).

B) Redwood error payload shape (REST)
We will standardize an “error” envelope with:
- error.type (string): fixed "overload_error"
- error.code (string): Redwood-specific code (enumerated; stable)
- error.message (string): human readable, safe to log
- error.param (string|null): optional (e.g., model), keep minimal
- error.request_id (string): request correlation id
- error.retryable ("true"/"false"): explicit signal for clients

We will keep message wording stable and non-alarming (no “outage” language unless it’s actually an outage).

C) OpenAI-compatible mapping
For OpenAI-compat endpoints we will map into OpenAI-style error objects without breaking common client assumptions:
- error: { message, type, param, code }
- HTTP codes must remain 429/503 as above.
- Redwood error.code becomes error.code, but we must also populate error.type with an OpenAI-expected category (e.g., "rate_limit_error" for 429) while preserving Redwood-specific detail in code/message.
- Ensure this does not break clients that branch on status code or error.type.

D) Retry-After semantics (and retry guidance)
- Retry-After is in seconds per RFC; provide integer values.
- We will recommend exponential backoff with jitter, and we will explicitly discourage tight loops and “retry immediately N times.”
- For 429: Retry-After is generally short (e.g., 1–10s) based on observed recovery time; subject to tuning.
- For 503 breaker-open events: Retry-After should be longer (e.g., 10–60s) when provided; otherwise omit and rely on standard backoff.

E) Deprecation / compatibility commitments
1) Status code stability
- Once shipped broadly, we treat overload mapping (429 vs 503) as part of the API contract. Any future changes must follow a deprecation policy (announce, document, provide migration period).

2) Body shape stability
- We will not remove fields. Additive-only changes are allowed.
- Code strings are stable identifiers; do not reuse codes for new meanings.

3) Header stability
- Retry-After will be the canonical retry signal; we may add Redwood-specific headers (e.g., x-redwood-overload-reason) but should not require them for correct client behavior.

F) Messaging principles (docs + support + status page)
- Overload protection is a safety mechanism; we should message it as “load shedding to protect latency and uptime.”
- We must clearly distinguish:
  (a) customer-side issues (client retry storms, misconfigured concurrency),
  (b) expected overload shedding during spikes,
  (c) true incidents/outages.
- Avoid blaming language. Provide actionable next steps.

G) Dedicated vs Hosted alignment notes (what is the same/different)
- Dedicated: shedding behavior may exist but should be less common; when it happens, semantics remain consistent (same 429/503 codes), but messaging should reflect that Dedicated has reserved capacity and may indicate customer-configured autoscaling limits / burst settings.
- Hosted: more likely to shed during regional spikes; supports fallback policies when configured.
- We need a short, explicit section in docs: “How overload errors differ between Hosted and Dedicated.”

Deliverables
- Finalized customer-facing behavior spec (this ticket) with sign-off from Product + SRE + Platform.
- Inputs to ADR-0147 (error taxonomy + HTTP mapping) and docs PR language.
- Support enablement bullets (what to say, what not to say), incl. Retry-After interpretation + billing note.

Open questions (resolved by end of this ticket)
1) Do overload errors count against billed usage?
- Proposed: No tokens are billed for requests rejected before inference begins. If partial generation occurred (streaming) we will bill for tokens actually generated; docs must state this clearly.

2) Streaming disconnect semantics
- Proposed: Prefer an explicit overload error over silent disconnects. Where transport constraints prevent a structured error mid-stream, we should still ensure clients see a clear signal (status + body when possible) and document limitations.

3) Fallback messaging
- Proposed: If fallback is applied (model/region), we do not change success response schema. We may optionally include a response header indicating fallback occurred (non-breaking, off by default).

Success criteria (product)
- Customers can reliably distinguish overload-protected failures from internal failures using status code + error.code.
- Support tickets about “mixed 500/502/503” under load decrease post-rollout.
- SDKs can expose retryability and Retry-After cleanly without requiring customers to parse message strings.

References
- Confluence ADR: adr-0147-overload-error-taxonomy-and-http-mapping
- Engineering umbrella: ENG-4821
- Error payload implementation: ENG-4823 / PR(s) in redwood + openai-compat repos
- Docs updates: ENG-4832
- SDK surfacing: ENG-4836

Requested reviewers / sign-off
- SRE: Rafael Mendes / Sean Gallagher
- Platform: Mina Haddad
- API semantics & compat: Brian Murphy
- Docs: Wei Chen
- Dedicated alignment: Lauren Bishop
comments: 2025-11-13 (Henry Cho): Drafted initial mapping: 429 for shed, 503 for breaker-open. Flagging one concern from Support: customers interpret 429 as “you exceeded quota.” We’ll mitigate by: (1) Redwood-specific error.code + clear message; (2) docs explicitly call this “temporary overload” and link to retry guidance; (3) keep quota/rate-limit errors as distinct codes/messages.

2025-11-14 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on 429/503 split. Important: we must be explicit that these are “overload-protected” errors so they don’t page as hard failures. Also, Retry-After needs to be conservative to avoid thundering herds; initial values may need tuning based on canary recovery times.

2025-11-15 (Brian Murphy): OpenAI-compat note: many clients branch on error.type == rate_limit_error when 429. Suggest: set error.type = rate_limit_error for 429 but keep Redwood detail in error.code. For 503, use error.type = server_error (or similar) but avoid inventing new types that break parsing.

2025-11-18 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated alignment: please add a doc note that Dedicated can still shed if customer sets max replicas too low or runs batch jobs that saturate reserved pool. But semantics should remain identical; only recommended mitigation differs (autoscaling/burst).

2025-11-20 (Wei Chen): For docs wording, recommend we avoid “circuit breaker open” phrasing in public docs; instead: “temporarily unavailable due to load; retry with backoff.” We can keep the technical term in internal runbooks/support notes.

2025-11-22 (Henry Cho): Added billing note proposal: no billing for requests rejected pre-inference; partial streaming billing based on generated tokens. Need confirmation from quotas/billing hooks owner (Cole Summers).

2025-11-25 (Cole Summers): Confirmed: gateway-side rejections won’t mint usage events; runtime mid-stream disconnects bill for tokens emitted. Please ensure error messaging doesn’t imply “free retries” and add guidance to cap concurrency to avoid retry storms.

2025-12-02 (Nikhil Sharma): Marking as approved. Please ensure PM-912 launch brief includes: (1) compatibility commitment (additive-only); (2) exact error examples for REST + OpenAI-compat; (3) one-paragraph Hosted vs Dedicated differences; (4) explicit retry guidance with jitter.
